The best initial experiment remains **content-conditioned retention inside GRU4Rec**, testing whether selectively attenuating recurrent history improves current-intent ranking. No improvement is claimed; the supplied inspiration’s 0.5338 score does not establish this proposal’s performance.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** (1) Users reject revived interests and weakly connected recommendations. Selective retention could address both, although neither gate values nor interaction histories provide observed intent labels. (2) Electronics has 9.7% wrong-order comparisons and a 0.0265 tenth-percentile margin. These identify difficult sampled comparisons, without establishing HR@10 performance. (3) Collapse scores near 0.5 imply near-zero mean cosine similarity. They provide no basis for an embedding-diversity penalty.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [MTAM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598) motivates recurrent retention, while [GRU-D](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-018-24271-9.pdf) supplies closer precedent for attenuating states before updates. Neither establishes gains for item-conditioned retention here. (2) [Correcting the LogQ Correction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) distinguishes always-included positives from sampled negatives. Objective changes require explicit sampling semantics. (3) [Ask the GRU](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.02116) supports jointly learned textual representations. Its setting does not establish sequential-benchmark gains. (4) [DIEN](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/4545/4423) modulates recurrent inputs or updates. Those mechanisms differ from scaling every previous-state occurrence inside a GRUCell.

The framework separates three directions: **state retention** controls historical influence; **ranking objectives** control competitor separation; **shared item representations** transfer supervision between related items. Test these separately before combining changes.

Scores are originality / potential / user alignment / model alignment / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder. Each assessment lists a positive and negative consideration in that order.

| Atomic idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Content-conditioned recurrent retention | 3/6/8/6/6 | Small, attributable state intervention; supports mechanism studies; targets stale and weak connections; may improve confusing comparisons; adds few parameters | State decay has substantial precedent; forgetting may erase useful history; intent remains unobserved; separation gains are unproven; custom recurrence complicates throughput and parity |
| Sampled listwise loss with uniform negatives | 3/7/5/8/4 | Established objective with a clear comparison; broad applicability; can prioritize stronger matches; targets Electronics separation; modest objective changes | Limited novelty; transfer remains uncertain; does not recover current intent directly; sampled separation need not improve HR@10; correction and exclusion semantics need care |
| Joint title/description mean-pooling encoder | 4/7/7/6/6 | Shares interaction supervision through content; supports sparse-item research; may strengthen identifiable media connections; can improve item discrimination; simple pooling architecture | Established hybrid principle; noisy text may dominate; generic words can reinforce broad relevance; sparse supervision may fail; preprocessing and serialization add work |

These are prospective judgments, not measurements. The revised retention ratings reflect closer state-decay precedents and greater implementation risk. At 0% progress, retain this bounded experiment; prioritize the loss alternative if measured recurrent-loop cost threatens the budget.

**Selected experiment.** Add a scalar retention gate before the corrected baseline’s GRU update, without importing the prior inspiration’s recent-history shortcut. Condition it on the previous state and current observed item embedding. This explicitly targets revived older interests and weak connections to current activity; improved state discrimination also targets Electronics’ wrong-order comparisons. Compatibility, redundancy, quantity and mood remain unverified.

idea.description: Add a content-conditioned scalar retention gate immediately before each GRU4Rec recurrent-layer update. Each gate uses that layer’s previous hidden state and current input; the first layer therefore conditions directly on the current observed item embedding. All representations and scores belong to one jointly trained network per category. This retains the GRU backbone and does not add an independently fitted predictor.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies revived older interests and weak connections to current activity as distinct recommendation failures. Selective attenuation could reduce obsolete state influence while retaining useful continuity. Electronics’ 9.7% sampled wrong-order rate and 0.0265 tenth-percentile margin provide model-facing targets. These mechanisms remain hypotheses: gate behavior and margin changes do not establish improved validation HR@10, actual intent recovery, product compatibility or reduced functional redundancy. State-decay precedents narrow the novelty claim, while the existing GRU gates make controlled attribution essential.

Modify the supplied corrected GRU4Rec rather than replacing its family. The supplied baseline code is not included in this report; implement against its actual resolved configuration rather than inventing dimensions, padding behavior or optimizer values. Record embedding and hidden dimensions, recurrent-layer count, projections, dropout placement, objective, optimizer, sampler, batch size, gradient clipping and checkpoint schedule. Retain them for the first comparison.

Use one scalar gate per recurrent layer and position: alpha_l = sigmoid(Linear(concat(h_l, x_l))). Initialize gate weights to zero and bias to 3, giving approximately 0.953 retention. This is a conservative initialization hypothesis, not baseline equivalence: repeated attenuation can materially change long histories. Compute proposed_l = GRUCell_l(x_l, alpha_l * h_l). Maintain a separate state for every recurrent layer. Upper-layer inputs have the baseline hidden dimension. Preserve any baseline input/output transforms and projections. Use PyTorch GRUCell rather than reimplementing gate equations; PyTorch applies the reset gate to the recurrent candidate projection, including its bias, and parameter order is reset/update/new. Moving reset before the recurrent matrix changes the model.

Copy each baseline GRU layer’s weight_ih_lk, weight_hh_lk, bias_ih_lk and bias_hh_lk into its corresponding GRUCell when establishing bypass parity. Match baseline inter-layer dropout, excluding the final recurrent layer, and disable dropout during evaluation. Preserve any additional baseline embedding or output dropout. Do not introduce recurrent-state dropout. Fused and explicit implementations need not consume identical training RNG streams; identical seeds do not guarantee identical dropout masks or optimization trajectories.

Skip state updates at padding positions in every recurrent layer using where(valid, proposed, previous). Zero embeddings alone cannot prevent bias-driven updates. Emit zero padding features after any biased output projection. Read the maximum index with sequence != 0, never count-1; preserve baseline empty-history handling explicitly. Inputs contain only observed history items, never their shifted positive targets. Keep log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items) compatible. This design needs no timestamps or reconstructed temporal inputs.

Maintain all four routes: Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Each category loads exactly one independently trained selected checkpoint. No checkpoint averaging, independent experts, auxiliary fitted popularity or transition scores, or inference fusion is permitted. Jointly trained gates and recurrent layers are components of that single network. Controls are separate trials and never fused at inference.

Sampled HR@10 against 99 negatives need not preserve full-catalog model rankings, and simulator responses from twenty training users are qualitative evidence rather than representative online utility estimates. idea.pseudocode:
class RetentionGRU(corrected_GRU4Rec):
    initialize(config):
        preserve_baseline_embeddings_transforms_and_scoring(config)
        cells = one_GRUCell_per_baseline_recurrent_layer(config)
        for layer in layers:
            input_dim = embedding_input_dim if layer == 0 else hidden_dim
            retain[layer] = Linear(hidden_dim + input_dim, 1)
            initialize_zero_weights_and_bias(retain[layer], bias=3)

    log2feats(sequence):
        valid = sequence != 0
        states = baseline_initial_states(sequence.batch_size)
        outputs = []
        for t in range(sequence.length):
            x = baseline_input_transform(item_emb(sequence[:, t]))
            for layer in layers:
                previous = states[layer]
                alpha = sigmoid(retain[layer](concat(previous, x)))
                proposed = cells[layer](x, alpha * previous)
                states[layer] = where(valid[:, t, None], proposed, previous)
                x = states[layer]
                if layer < num_layers - 1:
                    x = baseline_interlayer_dropout(x)
            feature = baseline_output_transform(states[-1])
            outputs.append(where(valid[:, t, None], feature, zeros_like(feature)))
        return stack(outputs, dim=1)

    predict_score(features, items):
        return baseline_scoring_head(features, items)

# Before full training, on bounded synthetic/public-history inputs:
# 1. Copy baseline GRU weights into cells; bypass retention with alpha=1.
# 2. Verify corrected padding policy, outputs, states, scores and rankings in eval mode.
# 3. Profile representative GPU steps with synchronized timing.
# These checks are distinct from the trained retention variant.

for category in supplied_four_categories:
    seed_training(42)
    model = RetentionGRU(resolved_baseline_configuration)
    for epoch in range(min(resolved_host_epochs, 200)):
        for step in range(200):
            batch = unchanged_family_sample_batch()
            loss = unchanged_baseline_objective(model, batch)
            unchanged_optimizer_step(loss)
        unchanged_validation_and_checkpoint_schedule()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint(category, model_configuration)
write_predictor_with_identical_architecture_and_routing()
verify_loaded_predictor_matches_selected_model_scores()

prediction(sequence, candidates):
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    positions = arange(sequence.length)
    last = maximum(where(sequence != 0, positions, -1), dim=1)
    # Handle last == -1 explicitly before gathering, using baseline empty behavior.
    return baseline_empty_handling_or_score_final_valid_feature(features, last, candidates)

# Controls are independently retrained alternative trials, never fused.
# Global-scalar control replaces each conditional gate with sigmoid(b_layer).
# Keep all diagnostic adapter signatures and measure actual model scores.

if host_exposes_paired_validation_hits:
    differences = variant_hits - baseline_hits
    for replicate in range(10000):
        category_deltas = []
        for category in supplied_four_categories:
            indices = analysis_rng.choice(200, size=200, replace=True)
            category_deltas.append(mean(differences[category][indices]))
        macro_deltas[replicate] = mean(category_deltas)
    interval = percentile(macro_deltas, [2.5, 97.5])
    # Use a cluster-preserving modification if users overlap across categories.

originality.positive: The item-and-state-conditioned scalar intervention defines a specific, attributable experiment against fixed recent-history pooling and global attenuation while retaining GRU4Rec.
originality.negative: GRU-D and time-aware recurrent models already attenuate previous states, and GRUs and DIEN provide related gating mechanisms. Novelty is incremental and an unverified exact match does not establish originality.

future_potential.positive: A small controlled intervention can support research on persistence of historical preferences across product and media domains, with explicit tests separating conditioning from global decay.
future_potential.negative: Additional attenuation may remove useful long-term preferences or act only as regularization. Sequence-only gates cannot establish intent, compatibility or redundancy, and sampled validation gains may not transfer to full-catalog utility.

code_difficulty.positive: The parameter addition is small, requires no new data pipeline and preserves sequence-only inference and one-checkpoint deployment.
code_difficulty.negative: Replacing fused recurrence requires careful multilayer state handling, dropout and padding parity, throughput measurement, diagnostic compatibility and exact predictor serialization; the engineering cost exceeds adding a linear layer.

related_work.title: MTAM: temporal gating for recurrent recommendation
contributions: Provides precedent for temporal gates in recurrent recommendation and short-term preference modeling.
limitations: Does not establish effectiveness of the proposed sequence-only gate.
Time gaps are not observed intent-change labels.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Distinguishes always-included positive items from sampled negatives when correcting sampled objectives.
limitations: Evidence from retrieval does not establish GRU4Rec HR@10 gains.
Sampling correction does not resolve false negatives or stale user intent.

related_work.title: Ask the GRU
contributions: Provides precedent for learning textual representations jointly with recommendation supervision.
limitations: Its collaborative-filtering setting differs from this sequential benchmark.
It does not establish that a randomly initialized lightweight text encoder improves the supplied baseline.

related_work.title: GRU-D: Recurrent Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series with Missing Values
contributions: Uses learned time-dependent hidden-state decay before recurrent updates, providing closer precedent for state attenuation.
limitations: Addresses missingness and temporal structure outside recommendation.
Does not establish benefits of item-content-conditioned retention in this benchmark.

related_work.title: DIEN: Deep Interest Evolution Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
contributions: Introduces attention-based recurrent mechanisms that modulate inputs or interest updates.
limitations: Its attention mechanisms differ from scaling the previous state before the complete GRU update.
Its click-through prediction setting does not establish gains under the pinned sequential HR@10 protocol.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog model comparisons.
limitations: Does not invalidate reproducible comparisons under the required pinned protocol.
Does not supply a correction that should replace the host evaluator.

related_work.title: Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse
contributions: Explains why repeated adaptive use of evaluation data can produce optimistic selection.
limitations: Does not quantify the selection bias of this particular experiment.
Ordinary paired bootstrap intervals do not implement an adaptive-data-analysis correction.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU and GRUCell documentation
contributions: Specifies GRU equations, parameter ordering, multilayer inputs and inter-layer dropout semantics.
limitations: Matching equations and copied weights do not guarantee identical training RNG consumption or fused-backend throughput.
Baseline-specific padding and scoring behavior still require explicit verification.

related_work.title: PyTorch CUDA semantics and timing guidance
contributions: Explains asynchronous execution and synchronized or CUDA-event timing for meaningful GPU benchmarks.
limitations: Measured throughput depends on actual model dimensions, sequence lengths, hardware and workload.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling, supporting preservation of model pairing within sampled users.
limitations: The four-category macro statistic and any shared-user clustering require explicit implementation.
Bootstrap uncertainty does not include unobserved training-seed or candidate variability or correct adaptive selection.
